pages.text: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → 4NO + 6H₂O on hot platinum - or, too cool or too slow, 4NH₃ + 3O₂ → 2N₂ + 6H₂O, which wastes it. The gauze must be white-hot and the contact a millisecond: long enough for the ammonia to react, short enough that the nitric oxide does not decompose. The NO is then oxidised to NO₂ and absorbed in water: 3NO₂ + H₂O → 2HNO₃ + NO.
$(thing)Set$(): Gauze temperature, Contact time.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Flow pulsing: the contact time varies by ±2%·d.

$(thing)Limits$(): The gauze is losing platinum (too hot); The gauze is below light-off: the ammonia does not burn.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Nitric oxide made: what burns, what burns the right way, and how fast the gas goes through.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Selectivity to NO: S(T, t)$(br)Ammonia burnt: X = 1 − e^(−t/0.2 ms)
